summary: Host scheduling of sibling tool calls in pi 0.85.1: the coding-agent uses pi-agent-core's legacy `Agent` + `runLoop` (NOT the newer harness). Sibling tool calls in ONE assistant message execute CONCURRENTLY by default (`Promise.all`, agent-loop.js:372) unless `config.toolExecution === "sequential"` or any called tool declares `executionMode: "sequential"` (agent-loop.js:287-291). The coding-agent never sets `toolExecution`, so the Agent default `"parallel"` (agent.js:134) applies. There is NO per-message concurrency cap, no semaphore, no global tool-call queue. All sibling results are awaited and appended to context before the next model request; only `tool_execution_update` progress events stream during execution. All siblings share one run-level AbortSignal (one AbortController per prompt, agent.js:330-340); nothing cancels siblings when one fails — a failing tool becomes an error result. A tool result MAY contain N image parts (type `(TextContent | ImageContent)[]`), all are forwarded to the provider; the only host-side normalization is a per-image resize (agent-session.js:260 → utils/tool-result-images.js) with maxBytes = 4.5*1024*1024 base64, max 2000x2000, JPEG q80 (image-resize-core.js:6-10); on resize failure the original oversized image block is passed through unchanged. No count/byte cap is applied to the tool-result array itself.

files.description: THE agent loop: executeToolCalls/executeToolCallsSequential/executeToolCallsParallel, runLoop, tool-result message creation (parallel by default).
Agent class: toolExecution default "parallel" (:134), single per-run AbortController (:330-340), signal forwarding into loop config (:299).
createAgentSession: `new Agent({...})` at :177 never passes toolExecution, and defines convertToLlmWithBlockImages (image stripping when blockImages is set).
_installAgentToolHooks (:~250-270): global beforeToolCall/afterToolCall hooks; afterToolCall runs normalizeToolResultImages on every tool result (built-in and extension).
normalizeToolResultImages: only host-side handling of image parts in tool results (per-image processImage, pass-through on failure).
wrapRegisteredTool/wrapRegisteredTools: extension tools become plain AgentTools via wrapToolDefinition, inheriting executionMode (no separate scheduling path).
Provider conversion: every image block of a toolResult is emitted (imageBlocks loop :1093-1102), no count cap.
convertContentBlocks (:80-112) maps all image parts of a tool_result to base64 image blocks, adding a placeholder text block when there is only image content.
ESTIMATED_IMAGE_CHARS = 4800 (:~172): each image part counted as 4800 chars in the context-token estimate used for compaction.

architecture: Prompt -> Agent.runWithLifecycle (one AbortController per run) -> runAgentLoop -> runLoop. Each iteration: streamAssistantResponse -> message.content.filter(type==="toolCall") -> executeToolCalls. Dispatch rule: sequential if config.toolExecution==="sequential" OR any called tool has executionMode==="sequential"; else parallel (functions collected in order, then `await Promise.all(...)`). In the parallel path, beforeToolCall hooks/validation run sequentially in call order; tool bodies then run concurrently; tool_execution_end and the ordered toolResult messages are emitted only after Promise.all. runLoop pushes all results into currentContext.messages and only then loops back to the model request. Tool calls and results are forwarded from AgentSession through the global agent hooks; extension-registered tools use the identical AgentTool path. ToolResultMessage.content is `(TextContent | ImageContent)[]`, copied verbatim into context (no truncation at the loop level); images are only normalized per-image by AgentSession's afterToolCall hook, and each provider adapter re-emits all image parts.
